speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture: Appearance is Reddish. Leukocyte Esterase is Positive. WBC count is 10-20 /HPF. RBC count is Too numerous to count. Nitrites are Negative. speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Serum creatinine, electrolytes, and blood count. Did you experience any severe pain episodes that made you sweat or vomit recently? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL, BUN is 14 mg/dL, and Complete Blood Count is within normal limits. The patient denies any severe pain episodes that caused sweating or vomiting. Renal ultrasound findings show multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla with no obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney. The ultrasound finding of multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts, combined with your history of recurrent UTIs and hematuria, is characteristic of this condition.
